speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are experiencing wrist pain and difficulty moving your hand; can you tell me exactly where the pain is located and what specific movements are difficult?

speaker: Patient
text: 34-year-old female. The patient reports experiencing pain in her right thumb and wrist, which radiates to her elbow for the past three months. The pain worsens when she holds her infant son and is alleviated somewhat with an ice pack. She mentions a history of falling on her right outstretched hand about six months ago. She also notes that her mother has a history of chronic joint pain treated with methotrexate. The patient has been taking ibuprofen as needed for her symptoms.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: De Quervain's tenosynovitis.

Thank you for the detailed history; the pain localized to the right thumb and wrist, radiating to the elbow, and worsening with holding an infant, is highly suggestive of tenosynovitis of the first dorsal compartment. Given your history of a fall six months ago, could you describe the specific mechanism of that injury and whether you noticed any swelling or deformity at the time? Additionally, have you noticed any stiffness in your wrist in the morning that improves with movement?
